statement: Hangul was created under King Sejong the Great (r. 1418-1450), completed December 1443, promulgated 1446 (Hunminjeongeum, a 33-page document, UNESCO Memory of the World register). The Hunminjeongeum Haerye, rediscovered 1940 in Andong, Gyeongsang Province, is a companion commentary directly explaining the featural design logic: basic consonant shapes are stylized diagrams of the articulatory organs producing each sound, systematized through a heaven/earth/human philosophical framework for vowels — an unusually direct primary document of a script's own design intent. Sejong knew of the concept of writing (Chinese characters were already Korea's established administrative/literary script) but designed original, non-derivative letterforms — the calibration case for STIMULUS_DIFFUSION combined with genuine novel featural design (⟨INFERENCE⟩: mapping this documented situation onto Kroeber's "stimulus diffusion" category, 1940, is this claim's own inference, not a term any cited scholar applies to Hangul verbatim).

sources.citation: UNESCO Memory of the World, "Hunminjeongum Manuscript" register entry.
